title: Acyclic pro-etale hypercover model for a bounded-below module complex
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with small pro-etale site and universes [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on that site, $W$ a site object, and $U_\bullet\to W$ a hypercover whose terms are weakly contractible, with these notions as in [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-affine-acyclic-hypercover]. Let $E^\bullet$ be a complex of sheaves of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] with $E^q=0$ for $q<N$, for some integer $N$. Define the total complex of $B^{p,q}=E^q(U_p)$, $p\geq0$, by $\operatorname{Tot}(B)^r=\bigoplus_{p+q=r,\,p\geq0}E^q(U_p)$ and differential $\delta+(-1)^p d_E$ on $B^{p,q}$, where $\delta=\sum_{j=0}^{p+1}(-1)^j d_j^*$ is the alternating face restriction. Each displayed sum is finite because $N\leq q\leq r$. Then there is an isomorphism in $D(R(W)\text{-}\operatorname{Mod})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], natural in $E^\bullet$, $$\operatorname{Tot}(B)\simeq R\Gamma(W,QE^\bullet).$$ Here $Q$ is localization at quasi-isomorphisms and $R\Gamma(W,-)$ means derived evaluation: replace $E^\bullet$ by a bounded-below complex $J^\bullet$ of injective module sheaves and a quasi-isomorphism $E^\bullet\to J^\bullet$, and take $J^\bullet(W)$. Existence of such chain-level resolutions and their K-injectivity are as in [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution]. In particular every quasi-isomorphism of bounded-below complexes induces a quasi-isomorphism of these total complexes.

proof.text: Construct the actual restriction augmentation alpha:E(W) to T(E), using the degree-zero row restriction and its (0,n) total inclusion.

Exact evaluation at each weakly contractible term and exact scalar restriction make every section column preserve quasi-isomorphisms. Finite-column truncation comparison gives T(f) quasi-isomorphic for every bounded-below coefficient quasi-isomorphism, and in particular for each given resolution map i.

The represented matching-map epimorphisms give local lower-simplex lifting. Transport the ringed site through ULiftHom and apply the existing ringed-hypercover injective augmentation theorem to prove each injective row quasi-isomorphic.
Use the single-column source and bounded-below row comparison to prove alpha_J quasi-isomorphic for every termwise-injective bounded-below J.

In the derived category take c(E,J,i)=asIso(Q(T(i))) followed by the inverse of asIso(Q(alpha_J)). Both isomorphisms exist by the preceding comparisons. The final conjunct is already the coefficient quasi-isomorphism comparison.

For the given homotopy i a ~ f j, use its cylinder: the cylinder is bounded below one degree below E, and its projection to E is a homotopy equivalence. Any functor that inverts bounded-below quasi-isomorphisms identifies the two cylinder inclusions, hence the two homotopic maps. Apply this to T followed by Q. The augmentation is strictly natural, so cancel its invertible image at L to obtain the displayed naturality equation. Resolution existence and K-injective representative selection are unnecessary because i,j,a and the homotopy are inputs. The generic cylinder argument is the existing helper now attached as lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-homotopy-invariance.
